purpose: Fictional service concepts for the start guide. These are illustrative images, not customer cases or automatically generated user projects.

images.prompt:
Create a polished high-fidelity fictional Korean web application screenshot for a service planning website's BEFORE/AFTER example gallery. Wide 3:2 landscape, flat front-on full-bleed interface, no laptop/phone/device frame, no perspective, no hands, no outside caption. This is a realistic product concept, not a wireframe or infographic. Art-direct a refined contemporary consumer service: beautiful editorial photography, spacious layout, crisp typography, restrained soft shadows, thoughtful icons, generous whitespace, beautifully aligned cards. Korean typography must be clear and use only the exact short text requested below; keep secondary detail visual rather than lots of tiny text. All names and data are fictional. No real company logos, no English lorem ipsum, no watermarks. Main interface should be usable-looking and legible when displayed at 700px wide.
Concept: neighborhood walking meetups, fictional brand "산책친구". Color palette forest green, pale sage, warm ivory and dark charcoal. Header brand with small leaf/path mark at left, navigation "산책 찾기", "내 모임", a round profile icon at right. Main title "가까운 이웃과, 가볍게 한 바퀴". Below small green chip "이번 주말". Main content features a large inviting wide photographic card showing a sunlit tree-lined riverside walking trail in Korea, a few tiny distant walkers with unidentifiable faces, lush greenery and warm morning sunlight. Next to it a refined meeting detail panel with title "토요일 아침, 한강 산책", simple calendar/time/location icons, short lines "토요일 09:00", "한강공원", "4명 참여 중", small circular illustrated avatar dots and prominent forest-green "참여하기" button. Lower row: two compact nearby-walk cards with smaller park photos, short titles "느긋한 공원 한 바퀴" and "노을 따라 걷기". Overall image should evoke a finished, welcoming walk-finding and joining service. Carefully balanced content at large scale, not a dense dashboard.
